relations.evidence: Clusters deployed on AWS support disk auto-expansion. For details, see [Storage Auto-Expansion](../clusters/scale-database.md#Storage-Auto-Expansion).

notable_absence.finding: AWS's own storage-speed/volume-type mechanics (gp3: 3000-16000 IOPS, io2: 3000-64000 IOPS, both independently configurable) are documented as pure infrastructure facts, not as a Capella behavior conditioned on AWS - contrast with Azure, where the equivalent storage-speed section explicitly states Capella's own configurability differs by disk type ('Premium storage disk speed... cannot be separately set. Ultra Disk speed can be set...'). AWS's version of this section reads as reference/spec-sheet content with no Capella-behavior claim to extract.

cross_component_finding: Tests this round's central hypothesis directly. Region tables, compute (vCPU/memory) tables, and EBS volume-type/IOPS specifics are pure infrastructure reference with no ontology value on their own - confirming the low-content expectation for this axis. But one genuine, well-evidenced exception survives: clusters:storage-auto-expansion is the SAME named Capella feature, cross-referenced to the identical 'Storage Auto-Expansion' target page, on all three provider pages - yet azure.json shows its mechanics differ under Azure specifically (node replacement/rebalancing with data movement) with no equivalent caveat on AWS or GCP. That is a genuine within-Capella cloud-provider behavioral difference, not just an infrastructure-spec difference, and it is exactly the kind of finding that justifies generalizing behavesDifferentlyUnder's range to a cloud-provider variant (cloud-provider:aws/azure/gcp) the same way deployment:capella generalized it to a deployment variant. The Multiple-Availability-Zones/support-plan gating, by contrast, recurs identically worded across all three providers - that pattern is provider-agnostic and belongs to the existing requiresSupportPlan axis, not a new cloud-provider axis.
